original_findings.title: Normal Anthropic finish_reason "end_turn" is classified as an incomplete response, so goal continuation never fires and the driver stops without running its gate
original_findings.evidence: `_prime_text_boundary` sets `terminal = ... or finish_reason != "stop"` (l.626) and `boundary_reason = incomplete_response(finish_reason=...)` (l.636-637). The only success value it accepts is the literal "stop". `AnthropicProvider.parse_response` (omega_prime/providers/anthropic.py:76-78) copies `stop_reason` verbatim into `row["finish_reason"]`, and a normal completion there is "end_turn". `ProviderModel.stream` defaults to False (providers/base.py:134), so this is the default Anthropic path. Scenario: goals or autonomous enabled, model is `ProviderModel(AnthropicProvider)`, reply has `stop_reason="end_turn"`. Then `terminal=True`, `turn_result["completed"]=False`, and `AutonomousDriver.after_turn` (agent/autonomous.py, `if not result.get("completed")`) returns `_stop(STOP_COMPLETED)` before `_run_gate`. The driver is permanently stopped after one turn with a gate never run. `rows` stays None, so an active goal with steps never gets its continuation prompt. The result reads `turn_exit_reason="incomplete_response(finish_reason=end_turn)"` and `completed=False`. Prime native uses "stop" and OpenAI-style providers use "stop", so only the Prime-native path and the tests (which hard-code "stop" or "length") exercise the happy case. No test covers a non-"stop" success reason.
original_findings.fix: Replace the `finish_reason != "stop"` equality with a set of truncation/abnormal reasons, for example `finish_reason in {"length", "max_tokens", "content_filter", "refusal"}`. Alternatively define `COMPLETE_FINISH_REASONS = {"stop", "end_turn", "stop_sequence"}` and treat only unknown values as incomplete. Add a regression with `finish_reason="end_turn"` that expects a goal continuation and the gate to run.
original_findings.requirement: LOOP-01 (active goal steers continuation), LOOP-03 (driver gate/limits honest), real gate diagnostics

original_findings.title: A stopped driver or stale stop_requested marker from an earlier run vetoes goal continuation and relabels every later public run
original_findings.evidence: `evaluate_autonomous` consults the live holder at every boundary of every run. If `holder['driver']` is a driver stopped earlier, `after_turn` returns `{action:'stop', reason:self._stopped}`. If `autonomous_stop` ran, `driver` is None and `stop_requested` stays True. `autonomous_start` is the only code that resets it (tools/autonomous.py:84; set at :101). Either way `_prime_text_boundary` sets `autonomous_stop` and reaches `if autonomous_stop is not None:` (conversation_loop.py:671-680) with `rows=None`, so `turn_exit_reason` becomes `autonomous_stop(...)` and `completed` False. Scenario: both families enabled. (1) The user runs autonomous mode until max_turns and it stops. (2) Later they call goal_set with steps and run a turn. Result: the goal prompt is never appended, because the old driver's sticky stop wins 'even with an active goal'. Every later unrelated turn also returns `completed=False` and `autonomous_stop`. The test at test_prime_loop.py:382-390 pins the sticky stop on the next run. The same-round precedence test (l.~440-460) is the intended case; the cross-run leak is not.
original_findings.fix: Scope the stop to a run that was live when this public run started or became live during it. For example, snapshot at turn start whether a driver exists and is running, and honor a stop verdict or `stop_requested` only if the driver was running at start or an autonomous_start/stop tool row appears in this run. Alternatively clear `stop_requested` once it has been reported, and ignore an already-stopped driver for continuation and labeling in later runs. Keep counters frozen, since a stopped driver still must not move.
original_findings.requirement: LOOP-01 (goal persists until paused/completed/cleared/stale/exhausted), LOOP-03 (stopped driver behavior), stale-vs-current precedence

original_findings.title: Boundary rewrites turn_exit_reason and completed to a stop reason even when no continuation was requested
original_findings.evidence: The cap override (l.655-659) and the goal override (l.660-664) run unconditionally after a successful 'stop' text response, regardless of whether anything wanted to continue. Scenarios: (a) hooks present with no active goal and a driver-less holder, and a normal answer lands on the last permitted call (`api_call_count == max_iterations`) or consumes a caller-supplied `IterationBudget`'s last unit. The turn is reported `max_iterations_reached(n/n)` or `budget_exhausted` with `completed=False`. Without hooks it is `text_response(...)` with `completed=True`. (b) A goal left paused, completed, stale or budget-exhausted from earlier. Because `GoalStatusView` is read fresh, every later unrelated turn is reported `goal_paused`, `goal_completed` and so on, with `completed=False`. A completed goal reads `completed=False`, which is pinned by test_externally_completed_goal_reports_on_the_result. `OmegaPrimeAgent._run_heartbeat_beat` and delegating callers cannot tell a normal answer from an unfinished one. The driver also receives `completed=False` for (a) and is permanently stopped as `autonomous_completed`.
original_findings.fix: Only override the loop's exit reason (and mark `completed` False) when a continuation was actually denied: some family had a continuation prompt or an active running driver. Otherwise keep `verdict.turn_exit_reason`. Keep the accounting unchanged. For the driver, pass the real completion of the turn, not `goal_reason is None` or the cap, when no continuation was wanted.
original_findings.requirement: Cap/tail paths, ordinary refusal vs successful content, default-off/message compatibility (hooks-on result shape)

original_findings.title: A continuation round vetoed before its model call erases final_response of the already-completed round
original_findings.evidence: `final_response` is assigned only when the loop breaks (l.343, plus the l.292 tool-round break). After a text boundary with `rows` (l.346-351) the previous answer is not stored anywhere before the next iteration. If that next iteration exits before a model call produces text, `final_response` is still None: interrupt or pause_gate (l.236-246), extension/before_model stop (l.247-254), or `account_output` failure (l.264-266, where the paid but dropped call is accrued by the tail path). `finalize_turn` then returns `final_response=""`, since `_stopped_on_tool_row` is False when the last row is the user continuation. Scenario: goal active with steps, round 1 answers 'part one', user presses interrupt (or an output budget trips) during round 2. The result is `interrupted=True, final_response=''`. The heartbeat runner (runtime.py `_run_heartbeat_beat`) returns `''` although a real answer sits in `messages`. Pre-change behavior returned the answer because the turn ended at the first text response. The dangling user continuation row also stays in `self.messages` with no assistant reply.
original_findings.fix: Remember `last_text = verdict.final_response` when appending continuation rows. For exits that happen on a non-tool tail (interrupt, before_model stop, output_budget_exceeded on a continuation round), use it as `final_response` instead of None. Keep the existing 'No reply: ... pending' close for tool-row tails.
original_findings.requirement: Cap/tail/provider-error paths, interrupt precedence, heartbeat returns actual final response

original_findings.title: Mixed total/component usage across calls in one logical turn undercharges paid work, and the test pins the undercount
original_findings.evidence: `sum_usages` sums per key, and `goal_token_delta_for_usage` / `_driver_usage` then treat `total_tokens` as authoritative when present. In test_usage_sums_tool_rounds_and_continuations_without_double_count (test_prime_loop.py:~190-226), call 1 reports `{prompt:4, completion:1}` (5 tokens, no total), call 2 reports `total_tokens:8` and call 3 reports `total_tokens:7`. The aggregate carries `total_tokens=15`, so the goal accrues 15 and the test asserts `tokens_used == 15` at test_prime_loop.py:225, although 20 tokens were paid. Call 1's 5 tokens are never charged to the goal budget or the driver. A single provider normally reports consistent shapes, so this is an edge case, but a call whose usage lacks a total next to calls that have one is exactly the 'charged once' accounting case.
original_findings.fix: Compute the budget delta per call (`goal_token_delta_for_usage` for each captured usage), sum those into a derived `total_tokens` used only for goal/driver accrual, and keep the raw key-wise aggregate for the public `usage`. Replace the test expectation with 20 or split the case so it does not pin the undercount.
original_findings.requirement: Once-only accounting; unknown usage stays unknown; lossless native rows

original_findings.title: Incidental wiring, default and wording pins in the permanent suite
original_findings.evidence: The consumer-visible flags-off assertions (identical transcript, no extra result keys, no scheduler threads) are good. These lines also pin wiring and defaults: `registry.runtime_bindings == {}` and `agent.prime_hooks is None` / `agent._heartbeat_runtime is None` / `session_name == 'default'` (l.636-640); `runtime.bindings['alpha']['runner'] is first._heartbeat_runner` and `is second._heartbeat_runner` (l.1033, 1071-1072), which assert forwarding identity through private attributes; and driver continuation wording `'Continue autonomously' in ...` (l.487), which is library text rather than a loop contract. test_lease_fast_fail_default_and_wait_opt_in waits a fixed `join(timeout=5)` on a deliberately blocked thread (l.671-672), a 5 s wall-clock sleep on every run. It cannot flake but it is slow. The l.1018-1100 heartbeat tests start a real APScheduler through `HeartbeatRuntime`, so thread teardown depends on `runtime.close()` in `finally` and on the 61-02 implementation.
original_findings.fix: Drop the private-attribute and default pins and assert the observable effect instead (a beat re-enters the owning transcript; a replaced agent's close leaves the replacement's beat working). Replace the wording assertion with a check that a second user row is present. Use an Event-based handshake instead of the fixed 5 s join.
original_findings.requirement: Test-quality constraint: no incidental wording/wiring/defaults pins; no timing probes

original_findings.title: Non-terminal boundaries permanently stop the driver with reason "autonomous_completed"
original_findings.evidence: Terminal accounting calls `driver.after_turn({'completed': False, ...})`, which sets `_stopped=STOP_COMPLETED`. This also happens for outer-cap hits, paused/stale goals, approval refusals and provider errors. Provider errors go through `_terminal_driver_stop` at l.~403-413, so a transient ProviderError kills the autonomous run. Tests pin `result['autonomous_stop']['reason'] == 'autonomous_completed'` for the cap, tool-tail, paused-goal and incomplete-finish cases. `turn_exit_reason` and `detail` carry the real cause, but a consumer reading only `autonomous_stop.reason` sees a success-looking value, and a later `goal_resume` or retry cannot revive the driver. This is the library's incomplete-turn semantics, so it is probably intended. Flagging it only because the contract asks for honest stop reasons.
original_findings.fix: If kept, document it in the result contract and have consumers read `detail`. Otherwise add a driver 'charge without stopping' accounting entry point for terminal boundaries.
original_findings.requirement: Honest stop reasons; paid work charged once at terminal/provider-error boundaries

original_findings.title: A malformed heartbeat row whose due_at and interval look valid re-fires forever (hot loop)
original_findings.evidence:
Scenario: a persisted heartbeat row has no session, or a non-string prompt, or an invalid interval (0, a string, or None), but a numeric due_at in the past. `heartbeat_set` does not type-check `prompt`, because `ToolRegistry.dispatch` does no schema validation, so a non-string prompt reaches the store.

The malformed branch (lines 543-548) calls `_finish_locked(store, job, now, None, outcome)`. Passing `interval=None` means `due_at` is never advanced.

It then calls `_sync_entry_locked` (line 548). That function only checks `_valid_due(due)` (line 727), so it re-adds an interval entry (or a `date` entry if the interval is invalid) with `fire_at = time.time() + max(0, due - clock())`, i.e. now.

The scheduler fires that entry immediately. `_run_claimed` takes the same malformed branch again, and the branch has no claimed_at or history dedupe. The result is an unbounded loop of disk rewrites, history churn and a `prime_degraded` event per iteration.

`start()` triggers it: the overdue pass runs the beat once, then the final sync (lines 343-346) adds the immediate entry. `test_missing_fields_skip_with_error` (test:608-642) builds exactly this row (no session, interval 60, due 1000). It asserts `len(service) == 1` right after `start()` returns, so it only passes because it checks before the scheduler thread's first re-fire, and `close()` then ends the loop.
original_findings.fix: Do not re-project rows that fail the same validity predicate `_run_claimed` uses. Factor out a `_row_runnable(job)` check and have `_sync_entry_locked` remove the entry and return when it is false. On the malformed outcome, either mark the row completed or errored so it is not re-armed, or advance `due_at` by a valid interval. Never schedule a `date` entry for a heartbeat row. Add a deterministic regression: after `start()`, wait for the scheduler to settle (or inspect `rt.job_ids == []`) and assert exactly one history entry and one sink event for the malformed row.
original_findings.requirement: LOOP-02/LOOP-06: malformed jobs yield one structured, redacted degradation without a runaway beat

original_findings.title: One out-of-range or non-finite due_at/interval makes every start/restart raise and leaves later rows unscheduled
original_findings.evidence:
`schedule()` validates `due_at` only by type (`_valid_due`, line 253) and persists the row via `schedule_heartbeat` before syncing. `_sync_entry_locked` (line 733) then runs `_at(time.time() + max(0, due - clock()))` and `add_job(seconds=interval)` with no guard. It catches only `ConflictingIdError`.

I confirmed with this repo's venv (APScheduler 3.11.3): `datetime.fromtimestamp(1.7e12, UTC)` raises `ValueError: year 55840 is out of range`, and `fromtimestamp(inf, UTC)` raises `OverflowError`. `IntervalTrigger(seconds=inf)`, `1e300` and `1e15` each raise `OverflowError`.

A model passing a millisecond epoch as `heartbeat_set.due_at` is a realistic trigger: the schema is plain `number` with no bounds, and `heartbeat.py` forwards it unchanged. Consequences:
- (a) With the runtime started, `schedule()` raises after the row is already persisted. The tool reports an error while the row stays on disk and shows up in `heartbeat_list`.
- (b) Every later `start()` (lines 343-346) and `_restart_locked` (lines 513-517) raises mid-loop, after `scheduler.start()` and `_started=True`. Rows after the poison row never get a live entry.
- (c) `OmegaPrimeAgent._attach` runs under `guarded_hook`, so the agent degrades on every construction until someone clears the row.
- (d) A failure inside `_finish_drain`'s `_restart_locked` propagates out of `unbind`/`stop`/`close`.
original_findings.fix: Reject non-finite or out-of-range `due_at` and `interval_seconds` in `schedule()` before persisting. Use `math.isfinite`, plus a datetime-range check or an upper bound on the interval. In `_sync_entry_locked`, wrap the projection and `add_job` in `except (OverflowError, ValueError, OSError)` and drop that row's live entry without aborting the caller's loop. Add regressions for `schedule(due_at=1.7e12)` and `schedule(interval_seconds=1e300)`, checking that other rows still start and the row can be cleared.
original_findings.requirement: LOOP-02: start/restart reconciles current persisted heartbeats. A bad row must not break other rows.

original_findings.title: Non-dict or id-less rows in jobs.json crash list_jobs, start and restart reconciliation
original_findings.evidence: `JobStore._load` keeps non-dict entries in `jobs`; it only does `setdefault` on dicts. `_find` guards with `isinstance(job, dict)`, but `list_jobs` (line 272), the `wanted` comprehension (lines 306-309), the pending loop (line 322) and the sync loops (lines 344-346, 515-517) call `job.get(...)` or `job['id']` unguarded. A row such as `"junk"` or `1` raises AttributeError, and a dict without `id` raises KeyError at `job["id"]` (line 322). The dependency `cron/heartbeat.py` has the same assumption: `clear_heartbeat` and `schedule_heartbeat` index `job["id"]` unguarded, so `runtime.clear`/`schedule` raise on such stores. The `list_jobs` AttributeError reaches the `heartbeat_list` tool, and the others reach the `start()` called by agent construction. The only malformed-store test is `test_malformed_store_raises` (`{"jobs": "nope"}`); it covers no row-level malformation.
original_findings.fix: Filter with `isinstance(job, dict)` everywhere runtime iterates `store.jobs`, as `_find` already does. Make `clear_heartbeat` and `schedule_heartbeat` use `job.get('id')` on dict rows only. Add a test that a store holding `['junk', {'kind': 'x'}]` plus one valid heartbeat still lists, starts and fires the valid beat.
original_findings.requirement: Malformed/foreign rows must be tolerated (LOOP-02, LOOP-06)

original_findings.title: Injected scheduler is silently restarted on a dead executor after stop/close/last-owner detach, and start() prunes unrelated entries from it
original_findings.evidence: `start()` (lines 299-301) and `_restart_locked` (lines 508-512) replace the scheduler only when `_owns_scheduler`. For an injected `scheduler=`, after `stop()`/`close()`/last-owner unbind, a later `start()` or `_restart_locked` calls `scheduler.start()` on the shut-down instance. In APScheduler 3.11.3, `BasePoolExecutor.shutdown` calls `self._pool.shutdown`, and a restart reuses the same pool. Every `submit_job` then fails; `_process_jobs` logs it via `logger.exception('Error submitting job ...')` and swallows it. The runtime still reports `_started=True` and `start()` returns normally, so beats never run and nothing is surfaced. The summary says injected schedulers are 'not silently replaced', but the dead-executor outcome is silent and untested; no test uses `scheduler=`. Separately, `start()` lines 311-316 remove every scheduler entry whose id is not a wanted heartbeat id. On an injected, shared scheduler this deletes non-heartbeat entries, contradicting 'foreign cron kinds untouched'. `_sync_entry_locked` does the same for same-id entries of non-heartbeat rows (lines 721-725).
original_findings.fix: For an injected scheduler, either raise a clear RuntimeError on start after a shutdown (no live executor), or document and test that the caller must supply a restartable scheduler. Restrict the prune loop and `_sync_entry_locked` removal to entries this runtime created, e.g. by tracking the job ids it added or using an id prefix. Add a test with an injected scheduler covering stop, then start, then a delivered beat or an explicit error.
original_findings.requirement: Restart: owned-vs-injected pool; foreign entries untouched

original_findings.title: Scheduler entries use APScheduler's 1 s default misfire grace, so a stalled scheduler drops the beat without catch-up
original_findings.evidence: `add_job` (lines 736-754) passes no `misfire_grace_time`. In APScheduler 3.11.3, `executors/base.py` `run_job` skips a run when `now - run_time > misfire_grace_time` (the default is 1 s) and logs 'Run time of job ... was missed'. A skipped run never calls `_fire_job`, so the claim/finish path is not entered and the entry is not re-synced. The scheduler's own next run is then `fire_at + interval`, while the persisted `due_at` stays overdue. Scenario: a VM or laptop suspend, or a stalled executor thread, delays an interval beat by more than 1 s. That beat is skipped until the next interval, with no history entry and no error. The code's design relies on `coalesce=True` plus the persisted-due guard to run one catch-up beat, and misfire skipping defeats that.
original_findings.fix: Pass `misfire_grace_time=None` (no limit) on both `add_job` calls, keeping `coalesce=True` and the persisted `due_at` guard in `_run_claimed`. Add a deterministic check, such as asserting the registered job's `misfire_grace_time`, or run an overdue entry through a paused-then-resumed scheduler.
original_findings.requirement: LOOP-02: persisted overdue beats are delivered once

original_findings.title: Permanent wall-clock native scheduler test remains
original_findings.evidence: `test_rebind_during_last_owner_shutdown_stays_live` uses a default real clock, `due_at=time.time()+1.0` with a 2 s interval, and `time.sleep` polling loops of up to 10 s (lines 1035-1036, 1050-1051) to wait for APScheduler to deliver. The phase constraint says wall-clock native scheduler probes are throwaways, not permanent tests. The SUMMARY says the timing-sensitive real due-now check was removed, but this one stays and is acknowledged only in the module docstring. It can flake under load: the first beat must start within the 10 s `entered.wait`, and the replacement delivery must arrive within the poll window.
original_findings.fix: Make the replacement-delivery assertion controlled: call `rt._fire_job(job_id)` after the rebind (as `test_last_owner_unbind_retry_preserves_replacement` does), or drive the injected clock, and drop the sleep polling. Keep only the Event-synchronised drain assertions.
original_findings.requirement: Tests: controlled synchronization, no wall-clock native scheduler probes

original_findings.title: test_missing_fields_skip_with_error is timing-dependent and masks HB-01; no test can detect a regression of due-now / injected-clock projection
original_findings.evidence:
(1) That test starts a real scheduler with the malformed row, which HB-01 shows is re-armed immediately. It then asserts `len(service) == 1` with no synchronization against the scheduler thread, so it passes only by the race between `start()` returning and the first re-fire.

(2) No test inspects the live entry's projected next-run time. Grep for `next_run_time` and `get_job(` in the file finds nothing. `test_restart_delivers_future_beat_after_stop` and `test_tracer_named_delivery` use an injected clock of 1000 with `due_at` in the future. If projection were wrong (a fire_at in 1970, or a full-interval delay for due-now), `_run_claimed`'s `due > now` guard would still reject early fires, so these tests would still pass. The 'due-now interval beat is not delayed one interval' and 'injected clock must not queue decades of missed fires' behaviors have no permanent regression.

(3) The file leans on private `rt._fire_job` and `rt._scheduler` (shutdown monkeypatch, `.pause()`), so real scheduler-thread delivery is never exercised without wall-clock use (see HB-06).
original_findings.fix: Add deterministic projection tests that read the registered entry's `next_run_time`, for example through `rt._scheduler.get_job(job_id)` on a paused scheduler. Cover: due in the past gives a next run no later than now plus a small epsilon; due at clock+N gives a next run about N seconds after now, not an epoch-1970 date. Add the HB-01 regression with a settle-then-count assertion instead of an immediate count.
original_findings.requirement: Tests: consumer-visible coverage of due-now and calendar projection

def dispatch(registry, name, arguments=None):
    result = json.loads(registry.dispatch(name, arguments or {}))
    assert not (isinstance(result, dict) and result.get('error')), (name, result)
    return result


def registry_at(root):

def wait_for(predicate, label):
    deadline = time.monotonic() + 8
    while not predicate():
        assert time.monotonic() < deadline, label
        time.sleep(0.005)


@contextmanager
def error_peer(failure_call):
    requests = []

    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def log_message(self, format, *args):
            pass

        def do_POST(self):
            body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers['Content-Length'])))
            requests.append(body)
            call = len(requests)
            if call == failure_call:
                payload = json.dumps({'error': {'message': SECRET, 'type': 'invalid_request_error'}}).encode()
                self.send_response(400)
                self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
                self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(payload)))
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(payload)
                return
            if call == 1:
                delta = {'tool_calls': [{'index': 0, 'id': 'call-fact', 'type': 'function', 'function': {'name': 'read_fact', 'arguments': '{}'}}]}
                reason = 'tool_calls'
            else:
                delta = {'content': 'native recovered' if call > failure_call else next(row['content'] for row in body['messages'] if row['role'] == 'tool')}
                reason = 'stop'
            chunks = [{'choices': [{'index': 0, 'delta': delta, 'finish_reason': None}]}, {'choices': [{'index': 0, 'delta': {}, 'finish_reason': reason}], 'usage': {'prompt_tokens': 9, 'completion_tokens': 3, 'total_tokens': 12}}]
            payload = (''.join('data: ' + json.dumps(chunk) + '\n\n' for chunk in chunks) + 'data: [DONE]\n\n').encode()
            self.send_response(200)
            self.send_header('Content-Type', 'text/event-stream')
            self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(payload)))
            self.end_headers()
            with suppress(BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError):
                self.wfile.write(payload)

    server = ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), Handler)
    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    try:
        yield f'http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_port}/v1', requests
    finally:
        server.shutdown()
        server.server_close()
        thread.join(timeout=5)
        assert not thread.is_alive()

observations: dict = {}

    log = ApprovalLog()

                "type": "function",

def tool_row(model, call_id="probe"):
    return next(
        row

mcp_stdio_smoke.source:
"""Exercise Prime tools through the real stdio MCP server (installed entrypoint).

Each call spawns a fresh `python -m omega_prime.mcp_server`, so state is carried
only by the on-disk root, exactly as a host would see it.
"""

import json
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from omega_prime.tools.mcp_session import mcp_session_call

REPO = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
ROOT = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="phase61-mcp-"))
for rel in (
    "omega_prime/contracts/tool-rosters/omega-prime.yaml",
    "omega_prime/contracts/policies/omega-prime.json",
):
    (ROOT / rel).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copy(REPO / rel, ROOT / rel)
(ROOT / "omega-prime.json").write_text(
    json.dumps(
        {
            "prime": {
                family: {"enabled": True}
                for family in ("harness", "goals", "heartbeat", "autonomous", "kernel")
            }
        }
    )
)
HOME = ROOT / "home"
HOME.mkdir()
APPROVED = ("harness_upsert", "goal_set", "heartbeat_set", "prime_cell")
COMMAND = [
    sys.executable,
    "-m",
    "omega_prime.mcp_server",
    "--root",
    str(ROOT),
    "--home",
    str(HOME),
]
for tool in APPROVED:
    COMMAND += ["--approve", f"{tool}:smoke-reviewer"]


def call(tool: str, arguments: dict) -> dict:
    out = mcp_session_call(COMMAND, tool, arguments, cwd=str(HOME), timeout=60)
    if "error" in out and "result" not in out:
        return {"transport_error": out["error"]}
    result = out["result"]
    text = result["content"][0]["text"] if result.get("content") else ""
    try:
        payload = json.loads(text)
    except ValueError:
        payload = text
    return {"is_error": "error" in out, "payload": payload}


steps = [
    ("harness_upsert scope alias", "harness_upsert", {"kind": "prompt", "id": "smoke", "title": "t", "body": "b", "scope": "global"}),
    ("harness_upsert valid", "harness_upsert", {"kind": "prompt", "id": "smoke", "title": "t", "body": "b"}),
    ("harness_list", "harness_list", {"kind": "prompt"}),
    ("goal_set stale_after_turns", "goal_set", {"objective": "ship", "stale_after_turns": 9}),
    ("goal_set blank step", "goal_set", {"objective": "ship", "steps": ["a", "  "]}),
    ("goal_set valid", "goal_set", {"objective": "ship", "steps": ["a", "b"], "token_budget": 100}),
    ("goal_status", "goal_status", {}),
    ("heartbeat_set bad interval", "heartbeat_set", {"session": "s", "prompt": "p", "interval_seconds": "soon"}),
    ("heartbeat_set future version", "heartbeat_set", {"session": "s", "prompt": "p", "interval_seconds": 30, "schema_version": 2}),
    ("heartbeat_set valid", "heartbeat_set", {"session": "s", "prompt": "p", "interval_seconds": 30}),
    ("heartbeat_list", "heartbeat_list", {}),
    ("prime_cell wrong type", "prime_cell", {"code": 5}),
    ("prime_skill_list unknown field", "prime_skill_list", {"bogus": 1}),
    ("prime_skill_list valid", "prime_skill_list", {}),
]
report = []
for label, tool, arguments in steps:
    outcome = call(tool, arguments)
    payload = outcome.get("payload")
    full = payload if isinstance(payload, str) else json.dumps(payload)
    report.append({"step": label, "tool": tool, **{k: v for k, v in outcome.items() if k != "payload"}, "payload": full})
    print(json.dumps({**report[-1], "payload": full[:200]}))

report_by = {row["step"]: row for row in report}


def code_of(step: str) -> str | None:
    payload = report_by[step]["payload"]
    try:
        return json.loads(payload).get("code") if isinstance(payload, str) else None
    except ValueError:
        return None


checks = {
    "harness scope alias rejected": code_of("harness_upsert scope alias") == "unknown_field",
    "harness scope alias flagged is_error": report_by["harness_upsert scope alias"]["is_error"] is True,
    "harness valid accepted": report_by["harness_upsert valid"]["is_error"] is False,
    "harness stored entry visible": "smoke" in str(report_by["harness_list"]["payload"]),
    "goal alias rejected": code_of("goal_set stale_after_turns") == "unknown_field",
    "goal blank step rejected": code_of("goal_set blank step") == "bad_value",
    "goal valid accepted": report_by["goal_set valid"]["is_error"] is False,
    "goal status has both steps": [row["text"] for row in json.loads(report_by["goal_status"]["payload"])["steps"]] == ["a", "b"],
    "heartbeat bad interval typed": code_of("heartbeat_set bad interval") == "bad_type",
    "heartbeat future version typed": code_of("heartbeat_set future version") == "unsupported_schema_version",
    "heartbeat valid scheduled": "scheduled" in str(report_by["heartbeat_set valid"]["payload"]),
    "heartbeat persisted and listed across processes": json.loads(report_by["heartbeat_set valid"]["payload"])["scheduled"] in [row["id"] for row in json.loads(report_by["heartbeat_list"]["payload"])],
    "kernel wrong type typed": code_of("prime_cell wrong type") == "bad_type",
    "kernel dir not created by rejected call": not (ROOT / "prime-kernel").exists(),
    "kernel unknown field typed": code_of("prime_skill_list unknown field") == "unknown_field",
    "kernel valid read-only works": report_by["prime_skill_list valid"]["is_error"] is False,
}
print(json.dumps({"root": str(ROOT), "checks": checks, "all_ok": all(checks.values())}, indent=1))
